title: introduce-node-quarantine-state-and-autoscale-hedging-policy-for-dedicated-fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Rolling upgrades and reactive maintenance currently cause SLO blips because nodes are either abruptly drained or left in open states where they accept new requests but have cold KV caches. We need a formalized node lifecycle state and a complementary autoscale hedging policy to guarantee throughput during maintenance windows and minimize tail latency impact for Dedicated customers.

Proposal: 1) Add a Node Quarantine state (RQ) between 'Draining' and 'Drained' that:
   - Stops accepting new allocation leases but continues serving existing connections in a degraded, metered mode.
   - Keeps KV cache warmed for a configurable grace period to reduce cache-miss storm when traffic shifts.
   - Emits observability signals (quarantine_start_time, warmup_remaining, served_tokens) for the Console.

2) Implement an Autoscale Hedging policy that:
   - Maintains a small reserved capacity buffer (hedge lanes) during scheduled maintenance windows and unplanned quarantines.
   - Prefers burst leases from Reserved Lanes first, then falls back to Quarantine-eviction flow to avoid SLO loss.

3) Add orchestration flow changes: a maintenance controller will move nodes through: ACTIVE -> PREPARE_FOR_QUARANTINE -> QUARANTINE (RQ) -> DRAINED -> REINTEGRATED, with hooks for KV warmup and latency-aware grace.

Why different from previous approaches: This separates acceptance of new leases from evacuation, allowing us to balance throughput guarantees and graceful cache handoffs. It reduces need for overprovisioned standby hosts and provides fine-grained, observable hedging that ties directly to Dedicated contracts.

Risks: increased controller complexity, potential for nodes stuck in RQ if controller crashes, and slight billing complexity due to metered degraded serving. Mitigations include transactional state transitions with retries, watchdog reconciler, and transparent billing notes in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Define Node Quarantine (RQ) proto/state and API surface for the orchestration controller
Controller transitions implemented: ACTIVE -> PREPARE_FOR_QUARANTINE -> QUARANTINE -> DRAINED -> REINTEGRATED
KV cache warmup window implemented and configurable per fleet/policy
Autoscale Hedging policy implemented and plumbed into scheduler with metrics-driven reserve calculation
Console shows quarantine metrics (count, avg warmup time, tokens served) and reserved capacity visualizer
End-to-end e2e test that simulates scheduled maintenance without violating SLOs on a 50-node dedicated pool
Documentation (PRD + runbook + SDK example) published and linked in ticket
